full_judgment: 10. It is difficult to follow the logic of the argument of the learned Advocate-on-Record for respondent No. 1. In a suit for partition the court will no doubt consider the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land in some details more than in a suit for  permanent injunction, but it cannot in either case convert itself into a court for determination of the respective titles of the parties if a serious dispute emerges from the pleadings as to the title of the plaintiffs to the partible property and if it is not possible to effect partition without formally determining the plaintiffs' title to the property claimed in the partition suit. Both the courts below concurrently held, without being reversed by the High Court Division, that the plaintiffs failed to prove settlement of the suit land with their mother Asia Khatun. If the plaintiffs are desirous of getting their full share as claimed in the present suit they must take the responsibility of proving their claim in a full-fledged suit for declaration of title. If the plaintiffs are driven to accept the deed of gift and the permanent alienation of the southern plot of the suit land to defendant No. 3, they must confine their claim for partition only in respect to the northern portion of the suit land in which the defendants admit the plaintiffs to be their co-sharers. The choice is with the plaintiffs but the way the suit was remanded leaves the appellate Court below with an impossible task. Its finding that the plaintiffs have not been able to prove settlement in favour of their mother remains unreversed. Its finding that the deed of gift was acted upon has been dismissed by the High Court Division by a slip-shod remark that it confusion worse confounded because the lower was based on "misappreciation of evidence". In other appellate Court will now have to re-write its own judgment, reverse its findings that (a) the plaintiffs failed to prove settlement in favour of their mother and that (b) the defendants' story of deed of gift is true and then give the plaintiffs full reliefs as asked for. That will be a judgment under duress without due reversal of the lower appellate Court's judgment by the High Court Division.
